{{Short description|Vertex adjacent to a leaf}}
[[File:Support vertex.svg|thumb|upright=0.75|Each blue vertex in the graph shown is a '''support vertex''', adjacent to at least one [[leaf (graph theory)|leaf]] (highlighted green). The darker blue vertex is a ''strong'' support vertex, and the two lighter blue vertices are ''weak'' support vertices.]]

In [[graph theory]], a '''support vertex''' is a vertex that is adjacent to a [[Leaf (graph theory)|leaf]] (a vertex of [[degree (graph theory)|degree]] one). Support vertices play an important role in the study of [[dominating set|domination]] in graphs, since every support vertex must belong to every minimum dominating set.<ref name="haynes2023">{{cite book |last1=Haynes |first1=Teresa W. |last2=Hedetniemi |first2=Stephen T. |last3=Henning |first3=Michael A. |title=Fundamentals of Domination in Graphs |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] |year=2023 |doi=10.1007/978-3-031-09496-5_2}}</ref>

== Definition ==

Let <math>G = (V, E)</math> be a graph. A vertex <math>v \in V</math> is called a '''support vertex''' if <math>v</math> is adjacent to at least one leaf of <math>G</math>.<ref name="haynes2023" />

A support vertex is called a ''weak'' support vertex if it is adjacent to exactly one leaf, and a ''strong'' support vertex if it is adjacent to two or more leaves.<ref name="raczek2025">{{cite journal |last1=Raczek |first1=Joanna |last2=Miotk |first2=Mateusz |title=Two Approaches to Constructing Certified Dominating Sets in Social Networks |journal=[[IEEE Access]] |volume=13 |pages=17495–17505 |year=2025 |doi=10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3532392 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Properties ==

* Every support vertex belongs to every minimum [[dominating set]] of a graph.<ref name="haynes2023" />
* If a graph has no weak support vertex, then its [[domination number]] equals its [[certified dominating set|certified domination number]].<ref name="dettlaff2020" />
* Every support vertex belongs to every minimum [[certified dominating set]] of a graph.<ref name="dettlaff2020">{{cite journal |last1=Dettlaff |first1=Magda |last2=Lemańska |first2=Magdalena |last3=Topp |first3=Jerzy |last4=Ziemann |first4=Radosław |last5=Żyliński |first5=Paweł |title=Certified domination |journal=AKCE International Journal of Graphs and Combinatorics |volume=17 |issue=1 |pages=86–97 |year=2020 |doi=10.1016/j.akcej.2018.09.004 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
* A tree <math>T</math> of order <math>n</math> has a [[Matching (graph theory)|perfect matching]] if and only if <math>\gamma_t^{\text{gr}}(T) = n</math>, where <math>\gamma_t^{\text{gr}}</math> denotes the Grundy total domination number. The characterization of trees achieving the lower bound for this parameter involves the structure of support vertices: among trees with no strong support vertex, the bound <math>\gamma_t^{\text{gr}}(T) \geq \tfrac{2}{3}(n + 1)</math> holds.<ref name="haynes2021">{{cite journal |last1=Haynes |first1=Teresa W. |last2=Hedetniemi |first2=Stephen T. |title=Vertex Sequences in Graphs |journal=Discrete Mathematics Letters |volume=6 |pages=19–31 |year=2021 |doi=10.47443/dml.2021.s103 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
